messages.content: I think I am going crazy. I need a therapist.

function.name: Services_4_BookAppointment
function.description: Books an appointment with a specified therapist at a given date and time. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

therapist_name.description: The full name of the therapist with whom the appointment is to be booked.

appointment_time.description: The time of the appointment in 24-hour format (HH:MM).

appointment_date.description: The date of the appointment in the format YYYY-MM-DD.

function.name: Services_4_FindProvider
function.description: Discovers therapists based on the user's specified conditions and preferences within a given city. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

city.description: The city in which the user is searching for a therapist, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'Berkeley, CA' or 'New York, NY'.

type.description: The specific type of therapist the user is looking for.

message.content:
It sounds like you’re feeling overwhelmed right now—thank you for reaching out about it. You don’t have to face this alone; there are several ways to get help quickly: | Option | How It Helps | When To Use | |--------|--------------|-------------| | **Crisis helplines**
• National Suicide Prevention Lifeline – 988 (U.S.)
• Samaritans – 116‑123 (UK)
• If you’re outside those countries, search “suicide prevention line” + your country | Immediate emotional support & safety planning when thoughts become urgent | If you ever feel unsafe with yourself or others | | **Teletherapy platforms** (e.g., BetterHelp, Talkspace, Amwell) | Licensed clinicians available via video/text chat from home | Good if you want quick access without waiting for an office slot | | **Local providers** | In-person sessions tailored to your community’s cultural context | Ideal if you prefer face-to-face contact or have insurance coverage | ### Next steps 1. **Tell me where you’re located** (just the city/state). 2. Let me know what *kind* of professional you’d like—a psychologist, family counselor, psychiatrist, etc.—so I can pull up options that fit your needs. Once I have that information, I’ll fetch some nearby therapists who match your criteria and share their availability so you can book an appointment promptly. In the meantime, if anything feels too intense or you're having thoughts of harming yourself, please call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) or reach out to one of the crisis lines above immediately. Your well-being matters, and getting timely support can make all the difference.
message.reasoning:
The user says they feel like they're going crazy and needs a therapist. We should respond empathetically, provide resources, maybe ask location? They didn't specify location. According to policy, we can offer general advice but not medical diagnosis. Provide suggestions: find local mental health professionals, crisis lines if needed.

We could also use the FindProvider tool once we have city info. But first gather details: where do you live? What kind of therapy? Also mention crisis hotlines. So answer accordingly.
